title: Opening a recording lands you somewhere you can work
goal: The way into editing a recording should be the shortest path from the thing you just captured to the thing you want to change, with no hunting and no empty window.
notes:
Build on docs/design/mocks/pages/video-entry-wt.html, whose opening line is the situation to design for: "No document open. The screen recording you made this morning is already in history, one keystroke away behind the menu-bar icon."

Deliberately independent of the time model so it can be done now: this is about the path in, not about what you land on.

---
Grounded in the video clickthroughs, which the user says are ideas to build on rather than specs: say in the audit where you went further or differently and why. The thesis every page shares governs this too: video is not a mode, it is the layer document with time.
acceptance: A recording in history opens for editing in one move from where you already are
What you land on is ready to work in: the clip is loaded, the transport responds, and nothing is dimmed waiting for something to finish
Opening something that is still being written, or that has gone missing, says so plainly instead of opening an empty window
Coming back to a recording you already edited puts you back where you were rather than starting over
Audit under queue/audits/ with the path from capture to editing captured, and anything rough filed as a follow-up
